results.input_text: We spent six months migrating our monolith to microservices and I'm here to tell you it was a mistake. Not the concept, the execution. We had a perfectly functional Django app serving 50k DAU with a P95 latency of 180ms. CEO read a blog post about microservices (I think it was the one from Uber) and suddenly we needed to be 'cloud native.' So we split the monolith into 11 services, added Kubernetes, added Kafka for event streaming, added a service mesh, added distributed tracing. Our infra team went from 2 people to 6. Our AWS bill went from $4,200/mo to $18,000/mo. Our P95 latency is now 420ms because of all the network hops. And we have a new class of bugs we never had before: partial failures, message ordering issues, split brain scenarios during deploys. The app serves the same 50k DAU. None of our customers noticed any improvement. Sometimes the boring architecture is the right architecture.
